The MakeHuman base mesh is released CC0, and MakeHuman's bundled system assets are generally CC0/CC-BY, but the specific licence of each bundled asset used here (afro01 hair, male_casualsuit06, shoes06, eyebrow001, eyelashes02) was NOT confirmed from within this environment.
assets.action_required_before_public_release: The project owner must confirm the licence of the MakeHuman assets used and add the required attribution. The baked 'www.makehuman.org' watermark on the t-shirt and hair textures should also be reviewed: it is visible in medium and close shots.
assets.modification_rights: asset NOT modified — every correction was made renderer-side in simulator/src/three/humanPresentation.js
assets.redistribution: held pending the licence confirmation above
assets.quality_gate: PASS — all 11 automated checks of simulator/tools/verify-human-asset.mjs.
assets.visual_review: PASSED with non-blocking limitations. Clean: face, eyes (brown irises correctly placed), closed mouth, ears, all ten fingers separated, wrists, and a fully bare forearm application site. Limitations: the card-based afro hair shows shell banding at face-close range, and the MakeHuman watermark is printed on the t-shirt.
assets.renderer_side_corrections: The export declares alphaMode:BLEND on ALL 9 materials (a Blender exporter default) even though the skin, suit and tongue textures have no alpha channel at all. Left uncorrected, three.js disables depth writing and the face stops occluding the teeth/tongue while the hair and eyelash cards paint black slabs over the eyes. simulator/src/three/humanPresentation.js restores opaque surfaces, alpha-TESTS the genuine cut-out cards (hair/brows/lashes) and the two-layer eye, and sets skin/eye/hair surface response. The GLB is untouched.

unblock_procedure.fastest_path: Ready Player Me (~2 minutes, free, no code changes)
steps: Open https://readyplayer.me and create an avatar (or use an existing one).
Choose a SHORT-SLEEVE / bare-arm outfit — the forearm is the cream-application area and must be bare skin.
Download / copy the avatar GLB URL and save the file as simulator/assets/human/human.glb
If it prints PASS, view it: cd simulator && python3 -m http.server 8080 -> http://localhost:8080/human-preview.html?model=human.glb
Record the source/licence in this file, then Phase 2 can start with no code changes.
alternatives: Any CC0/CC-BY rigged human GLB you can legally redistribute
Install Blender so a MakeHuman/MPFB CC0 model can be generated locally
Provide a direct licensed download URL on npm or raw.githubusercontent.com
